items.headline: Google will remove search for schools that reject AI features, drawing accusations of extortion
items.summary: Starting in 2027, schools using Google Classroom must accept AI features or lose Google Search entirely. Google says Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default but admits Search and AI are deeply integrated. Sen. Sanders called it extortion.
items.why: Google's near-monopoly on search in K-12 classrooms gives it unique leverage. Tying AI adoption to search access could force millions of students into AI-powered learning whether their districts want it or not, setting a precedent for how AI companies use market power to drive adoption.

items.headline: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, a cryptographic system to verify which AI model wrote a text
items.summary: FlashProve uses zero-knowledge proofs (zkSNARKs) to verify model identity without revealing weights. On Llama 4 Maverick (400B parameters) it generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second on a single H100.

items.headline: Anthropic expands text watermarking to Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, and Sonnet 4.6
items.summary: Text generated by these three models now carries a cryptographic watermark on supported platforms. On Sonnet 4.6, non-default temperature, top_p, or top_k settings may prevent the watermark from applying.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Message Threads beta, cutting time to first token by 35% on long conversations
items.summary: The API keeps conversation state server-side so each request sends only new messages. Threads stay encrypted in memory and expire after 5 minutes. Works across Claude platform, AWS, Microsoft Foundry, and Google Cloud.

items.headline: OpenAI shows GPT-6 Astra designing a hardware device from scratch in under a week
items.summary: Two engineers used GPT-6 Astra to design a Codex communication device with enclosure, PCB, firmware, and UI, with no direct human edits. A contract manufacturer built prototypes within a month. Partnerships with Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda expand the push into physical engineering.

items.headline: OpenAI appoints former Uber executive Jill Hazelbaker as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer
items.summary: Hazelbaker spent nearly two decades at Uber, Snap, Google, and in politics, most recently as Uber's President and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer. She will lead OpenAI's worldwide communications and corporate positioning.

items.headline: OpenAI hires former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for a national security role
items.summary: Driscoll resigned from the Pentagon after clashing with Defense Secretary Hegseth. The hire gives OpenAI direct ties to the national security establishment as AI export controls and model approvals increasingly run through the executive branch.

items.headline: Anthropic Q3 revenue hit $17B but compute costs consumed 58% of it, updated S-1 shows
items.summary: TechCrunch reports compute's share of revenue rose from 48% in Q2 to 58% in Q3, with the quarterly compute bill reaching $10B including $5B in short-term commitments. Revenue per compute dollar fell to 1.72x despite twelvefold year-over-year growth.

items.headline: OpenAI pushes to rename data centers as compute campuses and backs mandatory AI testing bill
items.summary: Semafor reports OpenAI wants data centers rebranded, compares AI rules to speed limits, and seeks bipartisan support for mandatory AI testing legislation. Brad Carson of Americans for Responsible Innovation called the rebranding Orwellian.

items.headline: Anthropic pitches Claude chip-design capabilities to IPO investors, The Information reports
items.summary: A 15-person in-house chip team uses Claude to design custom silicon for training and inference, claiming faster turnaround than standard workflows. Anthropic approached EDA firms about proprietary chip-design datasets. Synopsys and Cadence shares dropped nearly 4%.
